nodes.name: Polycondensation and Reduction
nodes.procedure: RuCl3 (1.000 g) was first dissolved in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) (50 ml) and placed on an ice bath in a three-necked round bottom flask. Hexaketocyclohexane octahydrate (HKH; 2.811 g, 9.006 mmol) was added followed by the addition of hexaaminobenzene trihydrochloride (HAB; 2.500 g, 9.006 mmol) under nitrogen atmosphere. The reaction flask was allowed to warm to room temperature for 2 h. The ice bath was replaced with an oil bath, which was heated to 175°C. This temperature was maintained for 8 h. After completion of the reaction, the reaction mixture was cooled to 80°C and NaBH4 solution (40 ml 10 wt% in NMP) was slowly added. The mixture was again heated to 175°C for 3 h. Then the flask was cooled to room temperature and the reaction mixture was precipitated in acetone. The black solid precipitates were collected by suction filtration using a polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) (0.5 μm) membrane. The resultant dark solid was further Soxhlet extracted with acetone for 3 days and methanol for 1 day, and freeze dried at -120°C under reduced pressure (0.05 mmHg).

nodes.source_text: The HER performance of Ru@C2N was first investigated in a 0.5 M H2SO4 solution... Ru@C2N shows a very small onset overpotential of 9.5 mV versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE)... exhibits the smallest overpotential at the current density of 10 mA cm−2 (13.5 mV in 0.5 M H2SO4 solution)... resulting Tafel slope of Ru@C2N is 30 mV decade–1... exchange current density of Ru@C2N was obtained (1.9 mA cm−2)... exhibited the smallest charge transfer resistance (43.7 Ω)

nodes.description: HER stability in 0.5 M H2SO4 after 10,000 CV cycles
nodes.source_text: After 10,000 cyclic voltammetry (CV) cycles, the polarization curve of Pt/C shifted negatively by more than 47 mV... In striking contrast, the polarization curve of Ru@C2N did not show any negative shift, instead it shifted positively approximately 10 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm−2

The HER performance of Ru@C2N was further studied in a 1.0 M aqueous KOH solution. Remarkably, it only took Ru@C2N a low overpotential of 17.0 mV to achieve a current density of 10 mA cm−2... showed a Tafel slope of 38 mV decade–1... showed excellent durability in alkaline solution, with negligible degradation

nodes.description: Active site poisoning test with SCN- in 0.5 M H2SO4
nodes.source_text: thiocyanate ions (SCN–) were introduced into the electrolyte (0.5 M H2SO4), which are known as metal-centred active site poisoners. The HER current of Ru@C2N decreased dramatically with the addition of SCN− ions

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM examination of Ru@C2N morphology (Supplementary Fig. 2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of Ru@C2N was examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM; Supplementary Fig. 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of C, N, O and Ru elements in Ru@C2N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed the presence of C, N, O and Ru elements...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows hexagonal Ru (PCPDF no. 89-4903) with peaks broadened due to small particle size and C2N overcoating; broad peak at 25.09° belongs to {002} plane of C2N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The indicated peaks in Fig. 2a can be attributed to hexagonal Ru (PCPDF no. 89-4903), while the broad peak at 25.09° belongs to the {002} plane of C2N... The broadened peaks are due to the small particle size and overcoating with C2N layers.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals Ru nanoparticles (average diameter ~1.6±0.5 nm) homogeneously distributed within C2N matrix with uniform size distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image (Fig. 2b and Supplementary Fig. 5)... the Ru nanoparticles (average diameter ~1.6±0.5 nm) are homogeneously distributed within the C2N matrix with highly uniform size distribution (Fig. 2b inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-resolution HRTEM shows Ru crystal lattice spacings of 0.234 nm and 0.214 nm attributed to {010} and {002} planes of hexagonal Ru viewed along <100> zone axis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spacing of the crystal lattices are 0.234 and 0.214 nm, which can be attributed to the {010} and {002} planes of hexagonal Ru viewed along the <100> zone axis.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS spectrum around Ru nanoparticle reveals presence of C, N and Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) spectrum (Fig. 2e) obtained at the local region around the Ru nanoparticle reveals the presence of C, N and Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS element mapping corroborates homogeneous distribution of Ru nanoparticles in C2N framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Homogeneous distribution of Ru nanoparticles in the C2N framework is further corroborated by scanning transmission electron microscopy coupled energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) element mapping (Fig. 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA shows Ru content of 28.7 wt% in the product.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru content in the product is calculated to be about 28.7 wt% from the thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) measurement in air (Supplementary Fig. 6).

nodes.characterization_summary: BET shows specific surface area of 400.1 m²/g, pore volume of 0.338 cm³/g, average pore diameter of 3.37 nm for Ru@C2N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area of the Ru@C2N was measured using the Brunauer−Emmett−Teller (BET) method, and indicated a specific surface area of 400.1 m² g⁻¹ with a pore volume of 0.338 cm³ g⁻¹ and an average pore diameter of 3.37 nm.
